correctedFields.value: Strongest feature: The move develops a transcript-grounded evidential expectation from divine capability and prospective self-disclosure, supplying materially relevant counterpressure against an uncomplicated personal-God hypothesis without merely denying transcendental grounding. Principal limitation: It never engages the decisive inference from logical attributes to a personal ground, while its debate-elimination prediction relies on substantially underspecified assumptions concerning divine intentions, noncoercive freedom, epistemic distance, and permissible ambiguity. Live burden: The hiddenness argument must identify the relevant disclosure intention, predict the expected distribution of reasonable nonbelief, and differentiate evidential insufficiency from persistent disagreement compatible with adequate revelation. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes genuine relevance to divine expectations, but also a targeted-grounding nonanswer, incomplete predictive specification, and an overextended inference from disagreement alone.

Strongest feature: The reply directly contests personal dependence by treating identity and noncontradiction as necessary across divine and nondivine possibilities, thereby engaging the grounding contention without disputing logic’s reality. Principal limitation: Imaginability remains an unreliable guide to metaphysical possibility, and asserting that logical truths persist without God neither supplies a truthmaker account nor establishes that divine nature cannot explain their necessity. Live burden: The position must clarify whether logic is fundamental, structural, conceptual, or descriptive, then demonstrate why positing a personal ground provides no explanatory improvement instead of merely restating independence. Locked score: The strong band reflects direct responsiveness, modal qualification, coherence, and pressure on divine dependence, while withholding credit pending a rigorous account of necessity and explanation.
